cityWatch.label: CITY WATCH
cityWatch.text: The BJP has announced a day-long demonstration at Freedom Park today, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., seeking rollback of recent milk-product and bus-fare increases.

lead.headline: BLUE LINE TRIAL REACHES OUTER RING ROAD; FIRST STRETCH TARGETS MAY 2027
lead.deck: A test train ran from Byappanahalli towards Doddanekundi on the IT corridor, a milestone for commuters awaiting the Silk Board–KR Pura section
paragraphs: Namma Metro’s Blue Line train reached Bengaluru’s Outer Ring Road technology corridor during a trial run on November 10. The train travelled on the up line from Byappanahalli depot to Doddanekundi, moving the project closer to mainline testing.

BMRCL is targeting May 2027 to open the 13-station Silk Board–KR Pura section, subject to testing and statutory clearances. The longer Blue Line will eventually connect south Bengaluru with Kempegowda International Airport.
Officials said the trial checks electrical systems, rolling stock and infrastructure readiness.

sidebarStory.headline: SC ASKS WHATSAPP TO DETAIL PLAN TO CURB DIGITAL-ARREST SCAMS
sidebarStory.subhead: The court also wants RBI proposals on fraud prevention and compensation for victims when banks fail due diligence
paragraphs: The Supreme Court has asked WhatsApp and other online intermediaries to submit proposals to prevent digital-arrest scams. It also directed state police chiefs to report cases and told the RBI to place its list of authorised financial institutions before the court.
The bench said banks should compensate customers when investigations find that a failure of due diligence enabled fraud; it cited ₹800 crore in reported losses to digital scams this year.

stories.headline: FIREWORKS ACCIDENTS IN BENGALURU TOP 150; BYSTANDERS ALSO INJURED
paragraphs: Reports from Bengaluru put the number of people injured in fireworks accidents above 150, with bystanders among those affected. Hospitals and eye specialists have urged residents to take precautions during the festival period.

stories.headline: SOUTHERN RAILWAY REVISES TIMINGS FOR 19 TRAINS THROUGH BENGALURU
paragraphs: The railway division has revised arrival and departure times for 19 trains operating through major Bengaluru stations. Passengers should check the latest timetable for their service before travelling.

stories.headline: FALLING CONCRETE AND IRON NEAR METRO STATION ALARM COMMUTERS
paragraphs: Commuters near Malleshwaram’s Mandhi Mall Metro station reported cement and iron falling from nearby apartment buildings. Residents have raised concerns about safety around the construction sites.

groups.ariaLabel: India diplomacy and public affairs news

stories.headline: INDIA PUTS BLACK SEA SHIPPING AND GRAIN FLOWS ON PEACE AGENDA
paragraphs: As Russia, Ukraine and the United States began talks in Abu Dhabi, India said it was engaging both sides on safer commercial shipping in the Black Sea, grain and energy exports, and possible non-attack arrangements. The proposals aim to reduce escalation and protect critical infrastructure.

stories.headline: INDIA REJECTS PANNUN CASE AGAINST NSA DOVAL AND EX-RAW CHIEF
paragraphs: The External Affairs Ministry rejected claims in a US civil lawsuit involving National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and former R&AW chief Samant Goel, calling the attacks on senior officials fabricated and malicious. India said the US midterm elections are an internal matter while stressing bipartisan support for bilateral ties.

stories.headline: CONGRESS TO HOST ‘BHARAT SUMMIT’ WITH DELEGATES FROM 70 COUNTRIES
paragraphs: The Congress is hosting an international conference with delegates from 70 countries. Party leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, global policymakers and figures from progressive movements are expected to participate.

groups.ariaLabel: India justice, travel, and education news

stories.headline: 18 TOURISTS INJURED IN SRINAGAR–SONAMARG CRASH; EIGHT CRITICAL
paragraphs: Eighteen tourists were injured in a road accident on the Srinagar–Sonamarg route, with eight reported in critical condition. Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha directed officials to ensure specialised medical care for those hurt.

stories.headline: HIGH COURT ORDERS CASE IN ALLEGED LIBRARY BOOK-PURCHASE SCAM
paragraphs: The Madras High Court ordered police to register a case and froze a publisher’s bank account over alleged irregularities in public-library book purchases. The inquiry began after concerns were raised about questionable authorship and inflated prices at a new Coimbatore library.

stories.headline: UPSC OPENS DAF WINDOW FOR 2,526 CIVIL SERVICES MAINS QUALIFIERS
paragraphs: Candidates shortlisted for the Civil Services Personality Test can submit or update their Detailed Application Form from November 11 through 25, until 6 p.m. The commission said interview dates will be announced separately.

stories.headline: INDIAN JUNIORS WIN FIVE MEDALS AT ASTRONOMY OLYMPIAD
paragraphs: Indian students won five medals, including two gold, two silver and one bronze, at the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics for Juniors in Thailand. The five-member team competed against students from 25 countries.

stories.headline: PARTLY CLOUDY TODAY; NO CITY WARNING IN FORCE
paragraphs: The India Meteorological Department forecast partly cloudy skies in Bengaluru on Wednesday, with a minimum temperature of 19°C and a maximum of 29°C. No warning is in effect for the city.
